claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name(s) of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 15 years old and lives with you.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather a bit more information.

Are you the parent or guardian with primary responsibility for Alex, and do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I'm Alex's parent and I do live in the UK - we're here in England. I'm the one who looks after Alex day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful.

Now, to continue with the assessment, I need to know: **What is your current employment or income situation?** For example, are you currently working, unemployed, or in some other situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working at the moment - I have a job. Why do you need to know about my employment situation? I thought Child Benefit was available to everyone?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question! While Child Benefit is indeed available to most families with children, there are certain circumstances where eligibility can be affected. One key factor is the level of income in the household, particularly if someone is earning above a certain threshold. This is why I need to understand your employment and income situation.

To be more specific: **What is your approximate annual household income, or alternatively, do you know if anyone in your household earns over £50,000 per year?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. No, I don't earn anywhere near £50,000 a year. My income is well below that threshold.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now, I have one more important question: **Is Alex currently in full-time education, such as at school or college?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still at school - doing GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility.

Let me review the key facts:
- You are Alex's parent and have primary responsibility for them
- You live in England
- Your household income is well below £50,000 per year
- Alex is 15 years old and currently in full-time education at school

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

You meet all the requirements:
- You're the responsible parent living in the UK
- Alex is under 16 and in full-time education
- Your household income is below the threshold that would affect your eligibility

You can now proceed with making a claim if you haven't already done so. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?
